source.title: Towards Reusable Network Components by Learning Compatible Representations
source.authors: Michael Gygli; J. Uijlings; V. Ferrari

record.file_problem: none; full paper and appendices are present.
record.tranche_reason: Tests component interchangeability and representational similarity using recombination accuracy and feature cross-correlation, rather than testing scale-dependent convergence with the original claim's measures.
record.gate_note: The paper measures whether feature extractors and task heads can be recombined, and measures feature cross-correlation. It does not sweep model scale or capability. Results cited from prior work are not included as rows. Several additional figure values are not reliably assignable to conditions in the flattened text and are omitted.
record.test_reason: The independently trained controls test direct component interchangeability, and the comparison of feature correlation with recombination accuracy bears on measurement dependence. Most other results deliberately induce compatibility and therefore do not establish naturally arising convergence.
record.authors_conclusion: The paraphrase is substantially accurate: the authors conclude that altered training can produce directly compatible components without compromising original-task accuracy, using joint or incremental training. Their correlation-versus-compatibility caveat is also accurately represented. They do not conclude that independently trained models naturally become interchangeable or converge with scale.
record.recipe_differences: The study trains networks with shared auxiliary heads or identical initial weights and evaluates task-head/feature-extractor recombination; it does not measure scale-dependent convergence or pairwise distance geometry as in the claim's original sources.
record.method_sensitivity: Recombination depends on batch-normalization evaluation statistics, split layer, number of common classes, initial weights, and joint versus incremental training. Cross-correlation and recombination accuracy rank methods differently.

fits_no_version.finding: Shared auxiliary heads and identical initialization induce above-chance or nearly lossless component recombination.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Networks can be trained deliberately to produce reusable, compatible components without reducing original-task accuracy.

fits_no_version.finding: Induced compatibility depends on normalization, split layer and the number of classes used by the shared auxiliary head.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: The effectiveness of explicit compatibility training depends on architecture, normalization and auxiliary-task coverage.

record.problems: The main compatibility analysis uses ResNet-56 on CIFAR-10 and STL-10, and several results are averaged across runs without numeric error bars in the text. It uses classification-head recombination rather than direct pairwise distance geometry. Some appendix figure values are flattened in the supplied text, so ambiguously assigned numbers were not extracted.
record.rows_left_out: Appendix B.5 per-dataset values for Figure 10 were not duplicated because the main Figure 2 aggregate results and the separately reported method-specific results are recorded. Figure 5 transfer-learning curve values and some Figure 6 normalization values could not be reliably assigned to specific methods from the supplied flattened text. Figure 8 split-layer plot is summarized only where the text explicitly describes the trend.

untested.parts: No scale or capability sweep, or test of increasing alignment across architectures, objectives and datasets with scale.
No isolated comparison of ordinary same-task training across random seeds establishing shared features or subspaces; the independent correlation experiment also changes training datasets.

Simple learned maps, post-hoc stitching, relative representations and unpaired mapping of ordinarily trained models are not tested. Positive compatibility results use explicit compatibility interventions.
No recurring interpretable feature or circuit analysis.
No neighbour-count sweep or direct test of representational convergence weakening on out-of-distribution evaluation inputs.
No scale-related plateau or causal comparison of shared data/objectives against a common-reality explanation. Intervention-dependent compatibility is insufficient to establish that explanation.

missing.what: Same-task independent-training control: Figure 7 reports 9.0% recombination accuracy on CIFAR-10. This adds a same-dataset failure of direct interchangeability beyond r1's cross-dataset control.

record.verdict_notes: The study is not an original source. Positive intervention results should not receive convergence-support verdicts. V6 is supported only for alignment preprocessing and disagreement between correlation and functional compatibility; its challenge direction calls for supports, not limits_scope. Partial channel correlation does not establish incomplete shared subspaces, and failed raw recombination does not rule out successful linear mapping.

versions.untested_parts: No model-size or capability sweep; no test of independently trained models with different architectures, objectives, data, and modalities becoming more aligned as scale increases.
No vision-language or paired image-caption models.
No study of shared features or subspaces across seeds in the same architecture as a naturally occurring convergence result; identical initialization is an intentional compatibility intervention.
Tests recombination of vision feature extractors and classification heads, but not linear maps, stitching layers, relative representations, or unpaired-data mapping.
No interpretable neuron, SAE feature, or circuit recurrence analysis.
Tests sensitivity to the similarity metric, batch-normalization statistics, network split, and number of shared classes; does not test out-of-distribution inputs or neighbour-count settings.

Tests compatibility induced by shared auxiliary objectives and initialization, and reports incomplete compatibility in some settings. Does not compare a common-reality explanation against shared training data/objectives, or test a scale-related plateau.

relation.reason: The study measures direct interchangeability of independently trained components and compares representational correlation with functional compatibility.

tranche.reason: Component recombination tests interchangeability through a different method; the independent controls and correlation comparisons provide relevant tests.

source_check.notes: The 10.6% figure is the observed independent-control accuracy, not a theoretical nine-class chance rate. Recombination uses test-batch normalization statistics; Figure 2 reports averages over 10 runs.

reader_labels.label: supports
reader_labels.condition: CIFAR-10/STL-10 recombination after shared compatibility training
reader_labels.reason: Shared auxiliary objectives and/or initialization make recombined components perform well above chance (r2–r8, r11).

reader_labels.label: supports
reader_labels.condition: same-task CIFAR-10 recombination and cross-architecture head transfer
reader_labels.reason: Recombination reaches within 1.1% of the upper bound in the same-task experiment, and transferred heads give high cross-architecture accuracy (r12–r15, r42).

reader_labels.label: limits_scope
reader_labels.condition: different CIFAR-10/STL-10 tasks and pretrained or incremental settings
reader_labels.reason: Compatibility remains below the upper bound, falls with different pretrained initializations, and is lower with incremental than joint training (r8–r11, r24–r27).

reader_labels.label: limits_scope
reader_labels.condition: similarity metric, normalization, split layer, and number of DCC classes
reader_labels.reason: Cross-correlation rankings do not match recombination rankings, evaluation normalization changes outcomes, later splits reduce compatibility, and fewer shared classes reduce recombination accuracy (r3–r7, r16–r23, r28–r42).

reader_labels.label: limits_scope
reader_labels.reason: Compatibility is often partial rather than perfect and depends on shared initialization, auxiliary training, and the quantity of common classes (r8, r11, r24–r27, r34–r41).
